welcomeSlides.title: Welcome, Doctor
welcomeSlides.body: We'll take you from here to your first day in an Australian practice, one step at a time. Here's how it works.

welcomeSlides.title: Job Search
welcomeSlides.body: Browse the practices matched to you. Apply directly to one you like, or send an enquiry if you have a question first.
welcomeSlides.note: You can have two applications in play at once, and three in a calendar month. Withdrawing from a position is final.

welcomeSlides.title: Meet the practice
welcomeSlides.body: When a practice wants to meet you, you'll pick an interview time that suits you. We arrange the video call and send you the link. Your Registration Support Officer joins you, so you're never in the room alone.

welcomeSlides.title: Offer and contract
welcomeSlides.body: If the practice makes you an offer, you review it here and sign the contract in the app. That secures your position.

welcomeSlides.title: Your registration unlocks
welcomeSlides.body: Once your position is secured, your personalised registration pathway appears: MyIntealth Account, AMC Portfolio, AHPRA Registration, Visa Application and PBS & Medicare. Our team guides you through each one, in order.

welcomeSlides.title: You never have to guess what’s next
welcomeSlides.body: We only show what you need right now. Your next step is always at the top of the page, and we message you when something needs you.

Australia Offers UK GPs More Than Just a Job

Australia needs experienced GPs. Across the country, patients need access to general practice. Communities need continuity of care. Medical centres need doctors who can manage chronic disease, provide preventive care, support families and build trusted relationships over time. This demand creates a strong opportunity for overseas-trained doctors. For GPs from the UK, Ireland and New Zealand, Australia can be a natural fit. Your clinical training, communication skills and general practice experience are highly relevant. Many practices are actively looking for doctors who can transition into Australian general practice and contribute long term. The need is not limited to one type of location. Demand exists in major cities, outer suburbs, regional towns and coastal communities. Some clinics need doctors because their patient base is growing. Others need replacement GPs because a long-standing doctor is retiring or relocating. In many cases, the demand is immediate. For the right GP, this can mean stepping into a role where patients are already waiting, the practice is motivated and the opportunity to build quickly is strong. The Expedited Specialist Pathway has made the opportunity more accessible for eligible doctors. With a clearer route into specialist registration, many experienced GPs can now look at Australia with more confidence. GP Link helps connect doctors with practices where the demand is real. If you are an experienced GP considering a move, Australia is actively looking for doctors with your skills.
Australia offers GPs a lifestyle built around flexibility, outdoor living, family time and career opportunity.
Australian GP income models give doctors more control over earnings through billings and practice choice.
Australian general practice can offer strong earning potential, especially in high-demand clinics.

Australian medical practices are actively looking for experienced, reliable and patient-focused GPs. UK-trained doctors are often seen as a strong fit for exactly that reason. General practice in Australia is built on continuity of care, communication, clinical judgement and the ability to manage a wide range of presentations. UK GPs usually bring strong experience in all of these areas. Many have worked in demanding environments, managed complex patients, handled high consultation volumes and developed strong communication skills across diverse patient groups. That experience is valuable in Australia. Many Australian practices are under pressure from patient demand. Clinics in growth suburbs, coastal communities and regional centres often need more doctors to meet local demand. In some practices, patients are waiting days or weeks for appointments. Practices want doctors who can settle, build trust and stay long enough to become part of the community. They are not simply looking for short-term coverage. They want clinicians who can contribute to the long-term strength of the practice. UK-trained GPs are attractive because their clinical background is usually familiar, their communication style often transfers well and their training is respected. For eligible doctors, the Expedited Specialist Pathway has made the process even more appealing. GP Link helps connect UK-trained GPs with Australian practices that are actively recruiting. If you are a UK GP considering Australia, the demand is not theoretical. Practices are looking for doctors like you.

Choosing the right practice is one of the most important decisions you will make when moving to Australia as a GP. The practice you join will affect your income, workload, supervision, patient base, support, contract terms, visa process, lifestyle and long-term satisfaction. This is why the decision should not be based on a single number or a location name alone. A strong Australian GP opportunity usually has several things working together: genuine patient demand, a supportive team, clear onboarding, fair commercial terms, good systems and a location that suits your life outside work. Some practices are very experienced in supporting overseas-trained doctors. They understand registration, supervision, onboarding, Medicare, provider numbers and the practical concerns doctors have when relocating. Others may be interested in recruiting but less prepared for what the process involves. That difference matters. A well-prepared practice can help you settle faster, start work with more confidence and build your patient base more effectively. A poorly matched practice can create stress, uncertainty and delays. Income is also closely linked to practice choice. A clinic with strong patient demand and good support can be far more valuable than a role that looks attractive on paper but does not have the patient flow to match. GP Link helps overseas-trained GPs compare opportunities properly. The right practice can set up your Australian career from day one.
Cities, coastal towns and regional centres each offer different lifestyle and career benefits.

Earning potential is one of the strongest reasons GPs consider Australia. Australian general practice often works differently from the UK. Instead of a traditional fixed salary model, many GPs work as independent contractors and receive a percentage of their billings. This creates a more direct relationship between the work you do and the income you can generate. For experienced GPs, this can be highly attractive. In a busy clinic with strong patient demand, good systems and a supportive team, doctors can build substantial income. Your earnings may be influenced by patient numbers, consultation style, billing model, hours worked and the percentage of billings agreed with the practice. Some clinics operate as mixed billing practices, where some patients are bulk billed and others pay a private fee. Others operate with a stronger private billing structure. These models can create different earning outcomes, and choosing the right practice is essential. The highest advertised percentage is not always the best opportunity. A clinic offering a strong percentage but limited patient demand may not produce the best result. A clinic with slightly different terms but full books, strong patient loyalty and excellent support may be far more valuable. GP Link helps overseas GPs understand the real opportunity behind each role. We look at the practice, patient demand, billing model, service fee and location so you can make a confident decision.

For many GPs, moving to Australia is not an individual decision. It is a family decision. You may be thinking about your spouse, children, schools, lifestyle, housing, long-term residency and whether the move will genuinely improve life for everyone involved. Australia is attractive because it can offer both professional opportunity and family lifestyle. Many doctors move not only because they want a better role, but because they want their family to have more space, warmer weather, outdoor living and a different pace of life. For children, Australia can offer access to schools, sport, beaches, parks and family-focused communities. For spouses or partners, the move can open new lifestyle and work opportunities depending on visa arrangements and personal circumstances. The location you choose matters. Some families prefer major cities with more infrastructure and schooling options. Others are drawn to coastal towns, quieter suburbs or regional centres where the community feel is stronger and demand for GPs may be high. The right practice should support not only your clinical work, but your transition into Australia. A good move should make sense professionally, financially and personally. GP Link helps doctors look at the full picture. We consider the practice, earning potential, location, family needs and long-term goals. For many GP families, the move is not just about working in Australia. It is about building a better future there.

For many overseas-trained GPs, Australia has always been attractive. The lifestyle, income potential and demand for doctors were already strong. What has changed is that the pathway is now clearer for eligible doctors. The Expedited Specialist Pathway has created a more direct route for certain internationally trained specialists, including eligible GPs with recognised qualifications. This matters because uncertainty is one of the biggest reasons doctors delay the move. When the process feels unclear, it is easy to put the idea aside. When the pathway becomes more structured, Australia becomes a serious and realistic option. For eligible GPs from countries such as the United Kingdom, Ireland and New Zealand, this pathway can make the move more achievable. It gives suitable doctors a clearer way to progress towards specialist registration in Australia and begin planning their move with greater confidence. The impact is significant. Australian practices are actively looking for experienced GPs, and many are ready to speak with doctors who are serious about relocating. The combination of strong demand and a clearer registration pathway creates a window of opportunity. The pathway still requires the right process, but it should not be viewed as a reason to hesitate. It should be viewed as a reason to start. With the right guidance, the steps can be managed in a structured and practical way. GP Link helps doctors move from interest to action. We help identify suitable practices, explain the process in clear terms and connect GPs with employers that understand overseas recruitment.

If you are a GP considering Australia, the best first step is to speak with someone who understands the process and the opportunities available. Australia offers strong demand for experienced GPs, attractive earning potential, better lifestyle options and a clearer pathway for eligible doctors through the Expedited Specialist Pathway. But the quality of your move depends heavily on the practice you choose and the guidance you receive early. GP Link helps overseas-trained GPs connect with Australian medical practices that are actively looking for doctors. We understand that moving countries is a major decision. You are not just choosing a job. You are choosing a practice, a community, a lifestyle, a visa pathway, a financial future and often a new life for your family. Our role is to make that decision clearer. We help you understand which practices are recruiting, which locations may suit your goals, what the income model looks like and how the opportunity fits your situation. We also help practices understand your background so the process can move forward properly. The right role can make a major difference. It can help you settle faster, earn sooner and build confidence in Australian general practice. It can also give your family a stronger foundation as you make the move. Australia is ready for experienced GPs. Practices need doctors, communities need care and eligible overseas-trained GPs have a real opportunity to build something better. Your Australian GP journey can begin with one conversation.

Life as a GP in Australia can be very different from what many overseas doctors are used to. The clinical work remains familiar. You are still caring for patients, managing chronic disease, dealing with acute presentations, providing preventive care and building long-term relationships. But the environment around the work can feel more flexible, more commercially rewarding and more lifestyle-friendly. In many Australian practices, GPs have the opportunity to choose their working sessions, develop areas of interest and build a patient base in a community that needs them. Depending on the practice, you may work alongside nurses, allied health, pathology, treatment room support and experienced administrative teams. Your week may feel more within your control. Some doctors choose to work full-time and maximise income. Others design a working pattern that leaves more room for family, travel, sport or outdoor living. The lifestyle outside work is a major part of the appeal. Australia offers beaches, national parks, outdoor dining, warm weather, sport, space and family-friendly communities. For many doctors, the change is not just professional \u2014 it is personal. Income can also be attractive. Because many GPs earn a percentage of billings, the right practice can offer strong financial upside. GP Link helps doctors understand what life in Australia could look like in practical terms. We help you compare practices, locations and opportunities so you can make a decision that supports both your career and your lifestyle.
Lifestyle, income potential, flexibility and long-term opportunity for overseas GPs.
Lifestyle, schooling options and long-term opportunity for GPs relocating with family.

Many NHS GPs are exploring Australia because they want a different way to practise medicine. The clinical work is still general practice. You will still care for patients, manage chronic disease, deal with uncertainty, build relationships and support communities. But the structure around the work can feel very different. Australian general practice can offer more flexibility, more autonomy and a stronger link between work and reward. Many clinics operate with a billing model where GPs receive a percentage of what they bill. For doctors who are used to a more fixed system, this can feel like a major change. It also gives doctors more control. Depending on the practice, you may have more say over your hours, appointment structure, clinical interests and working pattern. Some GPs choose to work intensively and maximise income. Others use the flexibility to create a better family balance. For NHS doctors who feel stretched, Australia can offer a new environment without walking away from general practice itself. You can continue doing the medicine you are trained for, but in a system that may offer more commercial opportunity and lifestyle flexibility. Australian practices often have strong support structures, including reception teams, nurses, treatment rooms, pathology services and allied health connections. Moving from the NHS to Australia is not about starting again. It is about taking your experience into a market where it is needed and valued.

More UK GPs are looking at Australia because the opportunity is no longer just theoretical. For eligible doctors, the move has become more realistic, more attractive and more achievable than it has been in years. Many GPs in the UK are highly experienced, clinically capable and deeply committed to patient care, yet they often feel limited by the structure around them. Heavy workload, increasing demand, administrative pressure and limited flexibility can make general practice feel more draining than rewarding. Australia gives many doctors the chance to practise medicine in an environment where their experience is valued and where the lifestyle outside work can be significantly better. Australian general practice offers strong demand for quality GPs across cities, coastal towns, suburban growth areas and regional communities. Practices are actively looking for doctors who can build relationships with patients, provide continuity of care and support local communities. For UK-trained GPs, this creates a strong opening. One of the biggest attractions is that Australian general practice can offer greater control. In many clinics, doctors work as independent contractors and earn a percentage of billings. This means income can be linked more directly to the work you do, the patient base you build and the practice you join. For motivated GPs, that can be a major shift from fixed or capped earning structures. The lifestyle is also a major factor. Australia offers warmer weather, outdoor living, beaches, space, good schools and family-friendly communities. For doctors moving with children, the appeal is not just professional. It is about giving the whole family a different quality of life. The Expedited Specialist Pathway has added momentum to this trend. For eligible GPs with recognised specialist qualifications, there is now a more direct registration route into Australian specialist practice. That has made the move feel less distant and more practical. GP Link helps make that move easier. We connect overseas-trained GPs with Australian practices that are actively recruiting and serious about supporting the transition.
Moving to Australia as a GP With Your Family

Moving to Australia as a GP is not simply about accepting a position in a different country. It is about choosing a different professional environment, a different lifestyle and a different long-term future. For many overseas-trained GPs, Australia offers the combination they have been looking for: strong clinical demand, attractive income potential, professional flexibility and a lifestyle that supports life outside the clinic. Australian general practice is built around community need. Across the country, practices are looking for experienced doctors who can support growing patient bases. Some clinics have full books. Others have long waiting times. Many communities simply need more GPs. This creates a strong opportunity for doctors who are ready to relocate and commit. The opportunity is not only financial, but the financial side can be compelling. In many Australian practices, GPs are paid based on billings rather than a fixed salary. That means your earning potential can reflect your patient load, working hours, billing model and the strength of the clinic you join. Australia also gives GPs choice. You may want to work near the beach, in a major city, in a family-focused suburb or in a regional community where demand is high. The right choice depends on your goals, but the range of options is one of Australia\u2019s biggest strengths. The Expedited Specialist Pathway has made this opportunity more accessible for eligible GPs. Doctors with recognised qualifications may now have a clearer route to specialist registration, making Australia a more practical option than before. Australia offers more than a role. For the right doctor, it offers a genuine upgrade.

One of the biggest advantages of moving to Australia as a GP is the range of locations available. You may be drawn to a major city, a coastal lifestyle, a family-friendly suburb or a regional community with strong patient demand. Australia offers all of these options, and each can be attractive for different reasons. City and metropolitan roles can offer convenience, schools, infrastructure, transport links and access to larger communities. For doctors who want to be close to major hospitals, universities, airports and established suburbs, this can be appealing. Coastal locations are often attractive for lifestyle reasons. Many GPs are drawn to the idea of living near the beach, spending more time outdoors and creating a better balance for their family. Coastal practices can also have strong local demand, especially in growing communities. Regional areas can offer some of the strongest opportunities. Many regional communities genuinely need more doctors, and GPs who are willing to consider these areas may find excellent patient demand, strong community connection and meaningful career satisfaction. It is also important to understand that the most familiar location is not always the best opportunity. Many overseas GPs initially think only about Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane or Perth. While these cities can offer good roles, some of the best GP opportunities may be in outer suburbs, coastal growth areas or regional centres. GP Link helps doctors explore the full range of options. Australia gives you choice. The right choice can shape your income, lifestyle and long-term success.

One of the biggest reasons GPs consider Australia is lifestyle. The weather is warmer, the days feel more open, and life outside work can be easier to enjoy. For many doctors, this matters. A career in medicine can be demanding anywhere in the world, but the environment around that career makes a major difference. Australia gives many GPs the chance to combine meaningful clinical work with a lifestyle that feels healthier, more flexible and more sustainable. Imagine finishing work and still having time for the beach, a walk, sport, family dinner outdoors or a weekend away. For doctors moving with children, the appeal can be even stronger. Australia offers space, schools, parks, coastal towns, major cities and family-focused communities. But the lifestyle is only part of the story. Australia is attractive because it also offers professional opportunity. Doctors are not moving only for sunshine. They are moving because practices need GPs, patient demand is strong and the right role can offer excellent earning potential. This combination is what makes Australia different. You do not have to choose between lifestyle and career. In the right practice, you can have both. Many GPs also appreciate the flexibility of Australian general practice. Depending on the clinic, you may have more control over your sessions, working pattern, billing style and clinical focus. GP Link helps doctors compare these options properly. We do not just look at the job title. We look at the practice, location, demand, earning potential and lifestyle fit.

One of the most attractive parts of Australian general practice is the income model. In many clinics, GPs work as independent contractors and receive a percentage of their billings. This means your earnings can be linked to the work you do, the patients you see and the practice environment you choose. For many overseas-trained GPs, this is a major shift. Instead of feeling that your income is disconnected from your workload, Australian general practice can create a clearer relationship between effort, demand and reward. If you join a busy clinic with strong patient demand, good support and an appropriate billing model, your earning potential can be significant. Doctors who build a loyal patient base, work efficiently and understand the Australian billing environment can do very well. There are different billing models across Australia. Some practices are bulk billing, some are mixed billing and some are private billing. Each model has different implications for patient flow, consultation fees and income potential. Mixed and private billing practices can be attractive for doctors who want stronger earning potential, but the real value depends on patient demand and clinic structure. Many practices may also offer an initial guarantee while a GP settles in. This can provide stability during the early stage while you build confidence in the Australian system and establish your patient base. For doctors who want stronger earning potential and more control, Australian general practice can be a very attractive move.
